incidents.title: Connection timeout on DB write – payments-api
incidents.error_messages:
psycopg2.OperationalError: could not connect to server: Connection timed out
DETAIL: server closed the connection unexpectedly
  This probably means the server terminated abnormally before or after processing the request.
WARNING: Write operations hanging > 30s on payments_transactions table
incidents.stack_trace:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app/db/session.py", line 48, in execute_write
    conn.execute(query, params)
  File "sqlalchemy/pool/base.py", line 310, in checkout
    raise exc
sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) could not connect to server
incidents.root_cause: RDS CPU at 95% caused by unoptimized query on payments_transactions table performing full sequential scan. A background job introduced a new query without an index on transaction_date + merchant_id columns.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Identified long-running query via pg_stat_activity (runtime > 1800s)
2. Killed the query: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) WHERE query_start < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 min'
3. Added composite index: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_txn_date_merchant ON payments_transactions(transaction_date, merchant_id)
4. Verified CPU dropped to 12% within 3 minutes
incidents.prevention_notes: Add CloudWatch alarm: RDS CPUUtilization > 80% for 5 minutes. Add query timeout of 30s to application config. Require EXPLAIN ANALYZE review for all new queries against tables > 1M rows.

incidents.title: Connection timeout on DB write – payments-api (recurrence 2)
incidents.error_messages:
psycopg2.OperationalError: could not connect to server: Connection timed out
psycopg2.DatabaseError: SSL connection has been closed unexpectedly
ERROR: write operations failing on payments_transactions
incidents.stack_trace:
sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) could not connect to server
  connection to server at "rds-prod.region.rds.amazonaws.com" (10.0.1.45), port 5432 failed
  FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
incidents.root_cause: RDS CPU at 92% again, this time caused by analytics team running an ad-hoc report query directly against production replica which replicated load to primary. Missing read-replica routing for analytics.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Blocked analytics team IP from production primary
2. Killed 3 long-running analytical queries
3. Redirected analytics queries to read replica
4. CPU recovered to 18% in 4 minutes
incidents.prevention_notes: CPU alert was added after previous incident but threshold was 90% (too late). Lowered to 80%. Analytics team must use read replica endpoint exclusively.

incidents.title: Connection timeout on DB write – payments-api (recurrence 3)
incidents.error_messages:
ERROR: connection timeout after 30000ms
psycopg2.OperationalError: SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected
PaymentProcessor: database write pool exhausted (pool_size=20, overflow=10)
incidents.stack_trace:
File "app/payments/processor.py", line 127, in process_payment
    result = db.execute(INSERT_PAYMENT_SQL, payment_data)
File "sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 3442, in execute
    return self._execute_context(dialect, constructor, statement, parameters, *args)
sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 20 overflow 10 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30
incidents.root_cause: RDS CPU spike to 88% triggered by a missing index on a new fraud-detection query added in v3.1.2 release (deployed 2 hours prior). Index on user_id + created_at was missing on fraud_signals table.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Rolled back fraud detection feature flag via LaunchDarkly
2. CPU dropped immediately to 15%
3. Added missing index on fraud_signals table in staging
4. Proper fix deployed as v3.1.3 with index in migration
incidents.prevention_notes: All database migrations must include index analysis. Add pre-deployment automated EXPLAIN ANALYZE check via CI/CD. RDS CPU alert threshold confirmed at 80%.

incidents.title: Connection timeout on DB write – checkout-worker (recurrence 4)
incidents.error_messages:
TimeoutError: DB write timeout after 30s
ERROR: statement timeout: 30000ms
High CPU alarm triggered: RDS CPUUtilization 97%
DEBUG: 847 connections in pg_stat_activity, 612 idle in transaction
incidents.stack_trace:
at DBPool.checkout (pool.js:234)
at OrderService.saveOrder (order-service.js:89)
at CheckoutWorker.processOrder (worker.js:156)
Error: Connection pool timeout: no available connections after 30000ms
incidents.root_cause: RDS CPU at 97%. A batch job processing 50k old orders for end-of-quarter reporting ran without pagination or query timeout, consuming all DB connections. 612 connections idle-in-transaction.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Found batch job via pg_stat_activity – idle_in_transaction for >45 min
2. Killed batch job process
3. SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '5min' on RDS
4. Rewrote batch job with pagination (1000 rows/page) and deployed
incidents.prevention_notes: Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout RDS parameter. Add connection pool monitoring. Batch jobs must have pagination and a maximum runtime limit. Recurring quarterly jobs need load testing.

incidents.title: Memory leak in checkout-worker after Node.js 18→20 upgrade
incidents.error_messages:
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
<--- Last few GCs --->
[1234:0x5601e4a200c0]   123456 ms: Mark-sweep (reduce) 1830.1 (1847.2) -> 1830.1 (1847.2) MB
ERROR: checkout-worker OOMKilled
incidents.stack_trace:
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
Writing Node.js report to file: report.1234.json
Node.js report completed
Aborted (core dumped)
incidents.root_cause: Node.js 20 changed the V8 garbage collection tuning defaults. The checkout-worker uses a large in-memory cache (LRU) that was previously collected aggressively under Node 18 GC. Under Node 20, heap grew unbounded under load until OOM.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Rolled back checkout-worker to Node 18 image immediately
2. Added --max-old-space-size=512 to Node startup flags as temporary fix
3. Profiled heap with clinic.js – found LRU cache never evicting under new GC
4. Fixed LRU cache TTL from null to 300s and redeployed with Node 20
incidents.prevention_notes: Test Node.js major upgrades with heap profiling under production-like load before deploy. Monitor heap_used_bytes metric. Add OOM alert at 85% heap utilization.

incidents.title: auth-service 503 errors after DB connection pool config change
incidents.error_messages:
HTTPException: 503 Service Unavailable – auth-service
sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 5 overflow 10 reached
ERROR: All connections in pool exhausted – new requests failing
incidents.stack_trace:
File "auth/middleware.py", line 34, in authenticate
    user = await db.get_user(token)
File "auth/db.py", line 89, in get_user
    async with pool.acquire() as conn:
asyncpg.exceptions.TooManyConnectionsError: remaining connection slots are reserved
incidents.root_cause: DB connection pool_size was changed from 20 to 5 in a config PR that was intended for the staging environment. The change was accidentally applied to production 2 hours before the incident.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Identified config change in last 4 hours of git history
2. Reverted pool_size to 20 via config deploy
3. auth-service recovered within 60 seconds
incidents.prevention_notes: Add config drift detection. Environment-specific config files must be clearly separated. Add a CI check that prevents staging-only values from reaching production.

incidents.title: search-indexer OOM after Elasticsearch JVM heap config change
incidents.error_messages:
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
[2024-07-14T03:22:15] search-indexer: container OOMKilled
ERROR: bulk indexing failed – heap pressure > 95%
incidents.stack_trace:
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded
	at org.elasticsearch.common.bytes.BytesReference.toBytes(BytesReference.java:129)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.bulk.BulkProcessor.execute(BulkProcessor.java:389)
incidents.root_cause: Elasticsearch JVM heap was changed from 4g to 2g in an infrastructure PR to reduce costs, applied 2.5 hours before the incident. Under normal load, 2g was insufficient for bulk indexing operations.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Restored JVM heap to 4g via Terraform
2. Restarted search-indexer to clear queue backlog
3. Re-ran failed bulk index operations
incidents.prevention_notes: Infrastructure cost changes must go through SRE review. Add Elasticsearch JVM heap usage alert at 75%. Load test configuration changes before production apply.

incidents.title: payments-api rate limiting cascade after Redis connection timeout
incidents.error_messages:
redis.exceptions.TimeoutError: Timeout reading from socket
ERROR: Rate limiter unavailable – falling back to allow-all mode
WARNING: 45,000 requests/minute to payments-api (normal: 8,000)
ERROR: Downstream payment processor returning 429
incidents.stack_trace:
File "middleware/rate_limit.py", line 67, in check_rate_limit
    count = redis_client.incr(key)
redis.exceptions.TimeoutError: Timeout reading from socket (10.0.2.11:6379)
  (error '111: Connection refused')
incidents.root_cause: Redis instance ran out of memory (maxmemory policy was 'noeviction') causing it to stop accepting writes. Rate limiter fell back to allow-all mode, resulting in a traffic spike that overwhelmed the payment processor.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Restarted Redis (memory cleared)
2. Changed maxmemory-policy from noeviction to allkeys-lru
3. Added circuit breaker: if Redis unavailable, use conservative rate limit (100 req/min) not allow-all
incidents.prevention_notes: Redis memory alert at 80%. Never use noeviction policy for rate limiter caches. Fail-closed (conservative limit) not fail-open (allow all) on cache unavailability.

incidents.title: auth-service JWT verification failure after certificate rotation
incidents.error_messages:
jwt.exceptions.InvalidSignatureError: Signature verification failed
ERROR: 100% of auth tokens rejected – all users logged out
authentication: [CRITICAL] JWT public key mismatch
incidents.stack_trace:
File "auth/jwt_validator.py", line 45, in verify_token
    jwt.decode(token, public_key, algorithms=['RS256'])
jwt.exceptions.InvalidSignatureError: Signature verification failed
jwt.exceptions.DecodeError: Invalid crypto padding
incidents.root_cause: Certificate rotation updated the private key in the auth-service but the public key in the api-gateway was not rotated simultaneously. All tokens signed with the new private key were rejected by the gateway.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Identified key mismatch via auth service logs
2. Emergency deployment of new public key to api-gateway
3. All services accepting tokens within 12 minutes
incidents.prevention_notes: Certificate rotation must be coordinated across all services simultaneously. Create a rotation runbook. Add a pre-rotation validation step that checks key consistency across services.

incidents.title: checkout-worker dead letter queue overflow – silent order loss
incidents.error_messages:
SQS DLQ: 15,000 messages in dead letter queue
ERROR: checkout-worker failed to process order: PaymentServiceUnavailable
WARNING: Orders silently dropped after 3 retry attempts
incidents.stack_trace:
File "worker/checkout.py", line 203, in process_order
    payment_result = payments_client.charge(order)
requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='payments-api', port=443): Max retries exceeded
boto3.exceptions.SQS.Client.exceptions.OverLimit: The maximum number of in-flight messages has been reached
incidents.root_cause: payments-api was down for 8 minutes due to an unrelated deploy failure. checkout-worker retried 3 times and sent orders to DLQ. No alert existed for DLQ depth. 847 orders were in DLQ when discovered manually.
incidents.resolution_steps:
1. Fixed payments-api deployment issue
2. Replayed all 847 DLQ messages
3. Manually verified no duplicate charges
4. Added DLQ depth CloudWatch alarm
incidents.prevention_notes: Every SQS queue must have a DLQ depth alarm. Add idempotency keys to payment operations. DLQ replay must be tested in staging. Add business metrics alert: orders/minute drops.

incidents.title: search-indexer falling behind – 6-hour index lag
incidents.error_messages:
WARN: search index lag = 21600 seconds (6 hours)
ERROR: Elasticsearch bulk write rejected – circuit breaker open
INFO: Indexing queue depth: 2.4M documents
incidents.root_cause: Elasticsearch disk usage hit 95% (flood-stage watermark), triggering read-only mode on all indices. A product catalog update the previous day added 8 million new product images, consuming 180GB of unexpected disk space.
incidents.prevention_notes: Add Elasticsearch disk alert at 70%. Product catalog updates must include disk capacity estimation. Set up ILM (Index Lifecycle Management) for automatic shard management.
